findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User-data is stored in Terraform configuration/state and can be retrieved by principals with instance or EC2 user-data access, exposing reusable credentials.

TCP port 22 is open from 0.0.0.0/0. Because portal_server is launched in a subnet that assigns public IPs and has a default route through an Internet gateway, the instance can be probed and attacked over SSH from any Internet host.

The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This gives the Internet-reachable instance unrestricted external connectivity, including a path to exfiltrate data or use the embedded AWS credentials if it is compromised.

The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key. Its contents, and the snapshot created from it, can therefore be stored unencrypted unless an account-level default outside this configuration happens to enforce encryption.
